summary: Douglas L. Berger works in philosophy, sinology, and indology. He was Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (attested 2007–2014) and Professor of Global and Comparative Philosophy and Centre Director at Leiden University (attested 2026).

Douglas Ober works in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington under teachers including Charles Keyes and Richard G. Salomon, and earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Harjot Oberoi (attested 2016).

Douglas Osto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a master's at the University of Washington (~1996–1998) and a PhD at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel (~2000–2004), later serving as Senior Lecturer at Massey University (~2007).
Douglas Q. Adams specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1968–1972) and held a post at the University of Idaho (~1972).

Douglas S. Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned his BA at James Madison University and his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins (~2000–2005), later teaching at East Tennessee State University (~2009–2014).
Dragana Majhen specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a master's degree at the University of Manitoba under thesis advisor Albert Welter (attested 2010).

Dragomir Dimitrov specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his MA and PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn (-2004), held habilitated posts there, and became Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

Dramdul works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Director of the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2004–2012) and editor-in-chief of Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2013–2020).
Drodul Dorji Tenzin studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Ayu Khandro, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Drolma is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Oslo, completing an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

id: P:Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé
summary: Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.
Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught figures including Sogyal Rinpoche and Keith Dowman.

Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Mindrolling and Dorje Drak monasteries under Sera Khandro and others, founded the International Nyingma Society, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Matthew T. Kapstein, and Alexander Berzin.

Dugald Mackichan (1851–1932) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Glasgow (~1866–1874). He served as Principal of Wilson College, Mumbai (~1884–1920) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1888–1891).

Duncan Ryūken Williams (b. 1969) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. After earning his PhD at Harvard University (~1993–2000), he held posts at UC Irvine (~1999–2005), UC Berkeley (~2005–2011), and the University of Southern California (~2011).
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed a PhD at Boston University under doctoral supervisor Malcolm David Eckel (-2001).
